title: Affineness descends along finite surjective covers of Noetherian algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be a Noetherian algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite surjective morphism with $Y$ an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is finite if every base change by a scheme is represented by a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Locally Noetherian means that an etale scheme atlas is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated. Quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Surjectivity is on the field-valued point classes with atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Then $X$ is represented by an affine scheme over $S$.

proof.text: Work on a small representative of the etale site in a universe containing the required objects. Grothendieck-abelian sheafification, with abelian-group coefficients, supplies sheafification of abelian presheaves and hence the hypothesis of the module forgetful lemma. For every module sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, set $\mathcal P(F)$ to mean $H^1(X,F)=0$, using underlying additive sheaves. Exactness of the module-to-abelian forgetful functor and the derived-functor long exact sequence give $H^1(X,F_1)\to H^1(X,F)\to H^1(X,F_2)$ exact for a short exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F\to F_2\to0$. Thus vanishing for the two ends implies vanishing for the middle. Also $\mathcal P(0)$ holds, and the property is invariant under isomorphism. For $r\ge1$, inclusion into the first summand and projection back give maps $F\to F^{\oplus r}\to F$ with composite the identity. Applying $H^1$ gives a retraction; if $H^1(X,F^{\oplus r})=0$, the identity of $H^1(X,F)$ is zero. These verify the zero, extension and summand hypotheses of coherent devissage.

Let $i:Z\to X$ be a reduced closed subspace with nonempty irreducible $|Z|$. Form $Z\prime=Y\times_XZ$, $f\prime:Z\prime\to Z$, and $i\prime:Z\prime\to Y$. The finite-cover structure-support lemma applies because $X$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ is finite surjective: $f\prime$ is finite surjective, $Z,Z\prime$ are locally Noetherian, and $G=f\prime_*\mathcal O_{Z\prime}$ is coherent with support $|Z|$. The structure-support statement also gives that $i\prime$ is a closed immersion on every scheme test. Test this with $\mathrm{id}_Y:Y\to Y$: since $Y$ is a scheme, representability gives a scheme representing $Z\prime\times_Y Y=Z\prime$, and $i\prime$ is a closed immersion of schemes. Writing $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the scheme closed-immersion description therefore gives $Z\prime=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq B$, so $Z\prime$ is affine. No assumption that $Z$ is a scheme is made.

Fix a nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$. Set $I\prime=(f\prime)^{-1}I\,\mathcal O_{Z\prime}$, the submodule generated by products via the structure map. Since $f\prime$ is finite, its scheme tests are affine. Apply ideal-product projection to the quasi-coherent structure module $\mathcal O_{Z\prime}$ to obtain a quasi-coherent ideal $I\prime$ and the identity of quasi-coherent submodules of $G$: $$G\prime:=IG=f\prime_*I\prime.$$ This is an equality of ideal products, with no assertion that pullback of the inclusion $I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Z$ stays injective.

The coherent-subquotient lemma on the locally Noetherian space $Z$ shows that $G\prime$, $G/G\prime$, and $\mathcal O_Z/I$ are coherent with closed support. Put $V(I)=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O_Z/I)$. Outside $V(I)$ the ideal has unit geometric stalk, hence $IG=G$ there, so $\operatorname{Supp}(G/G\prime)\subseteq V(I)$. This closed set is proper: nonzero $I$ has a nonzero section $a$ on an affine etale scheme chart of $Z$; the chart is reduced. In its reduced coordinate ring, $a$ is not nilpotent, so some prime avoids $a$ (the intersection of all primes is the nilradical). At a geometric point above that prime $a$ is invertible, so $I=\mathcal O_Z$ on that geometric stalk and the corresponding point lies outside $V(I)$. Thus $\operatorname{Supp}(G/G\prime)$ is proper closed in $|Z|$.

Because $Z\prime$ is an affine scheme and $I\prime$ is a quasi-coherent module on its small etale site, the Zariski--etale equivalence for the scheme $Z\prime$ gives $I\prime\cong(I\prime_{\mathrm{Zar}})_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the quasi-coherent Zariski module $I\prime_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ of its restriction to open subschemes; affine etale acyclicity applied to $I\prime_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ then gives $H^1(Z\prime,I\prime)=0$. The affine-map cohomology comparison for $f\prime$ then gives $$H^1(Z,G\prime)=H^1(Z,f\prime_*I\prime)\cong H^1(Z\prime,I\prime)=0.$$ The closed immersion $i$ is affine on every scheme test, by the quotient-ring description of closed immersions. Apply the same comparison to the quasi-coherent module $G\prime$ and $i$ to get $$H^1(X,i_*G\prime)\cong H^1(Z,G\prime)=0.$$ These are the two comparisons required by the source; affineness of the algebraic space $Z$ is not used.

Apply the corrected higher-rank coherent devissage criterion on the Noetherian algebraic space $X$ to the property $\mathcal P$. Step 1 verifies its zero, extension and positive-sum conditions. For every reduced irreducible closed $Z$, step 2 supplies the full-support coherent $G$. For each nonzero ideal $I$, steps 3--5 supply the quasi-coherent submodule $G\prime=IG\subseteq IG$, its proper closed quotient support, and $\mathcal P(i_*G\prime)$. Hence $H^1(X,F)=0$ for every coherent module $F$ on $X$.

Let $F$ be any quasi-coherent module on $X$. The coherent-filtered-union lemma gives a small nonempty directed set $D$ of coherent submodules and a canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_{d\in D}F_d\cong F$ in module sheaves. Choose a universe containing this subobject set and the small site. Write $U$ for the module-to-abelian forgetful functor. Abelian-group sheafification supplies its lemma's hypothesis, so the canonical map $\varinjlim_d U(F_d)\to U(\varinjlim_d F_d)$ is an isomorphism. Composing with the forgotten union isomorphism identifies $\varinjlim_d U(F_d)$ with $U(F)$ in abelian sheaves. Since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, filtered-colimit cohomology now gives an isomorphism $$\varinjlim_d H^1(X,U(F_d))\longrightarrow H^1(X,U(F)).$$ Each group on the left is zero by step 6, so the colimit and hence $H^1(X,F)$ vanish. Thus vanishing extends to every quasi-coherent module.

The Noetherian hypotheses include quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Step 7 proves the precise hypothesis of the algebraic-space Serre criterion, namely $H^1(X,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $F$. Therefore $X$ is represented by an affine scheme, with its given map to $S$, as claimed.
